subject: Request: Cloudport latency forgiveness and bespoke billing adjustment
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@cloudport.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency surge this week — request for usage forgiveness

Hi Avery,

We saw a sustained latency elevation in our US-west deployment window between Jan 12–13 that degraded our inference tail latency and caused throttling in our customer-facing flows. Engineering captured a perf trace and I attached a short timeline and the usage CSV for your ops team.

Our agreement has a 99.9% latency SLO for 95th percentile tail across the region; Cloudport experienced a 30–40% increase in p95 during the window, and it materially impacted our live traffic routing. Our procurement team has asked whether Redwood can provide some usage forgiveness or an ad-hoc billing adjustment for the impacted period while we work through a staging-based mitigation.

Can you outline the internal approval path and what a bespoke allowance might look like (e.g., partial credit, one free bursts month, or an invoice offset)? We need a formal proposal to take to our CFO by Jan 21.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Site Reliability
Cloudport

Attachments:
- incident-timeline.pdf (pdf)
- cloudport-usage-q4.csv (csv)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@cloudport.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency surge this week — request for usage forgiveness

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the timeline and the usage export. I'm sorry Cloudport ran into that window — we take these events seriously. I've looped in Karthik from Sales/RevOps to help with a formal proposal and to scope what we can offer quickly.

High level next steps from our side:
- Ops will validate the incident attribution and compute the affected token consumption window.
- Sales will propose a commercial remedy package (credit structure + optional free burst month) and route for exec sign-off.
- We'll aim to have a draft offer to you by EOD Jan 20 so you can review with your CFO.

Can you confirm whether the p95 impact you measured is for production requests only (not staging), and whether you'd prefer a percentage-of-usage credit or a flat-dollar invoice offset? That will help us model the options.

Best,
Avery
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Cloudport latency forgiveness and bespoke billing adjustment

Avery / Marissa —

Looping you both in. I ran a quick look at Cloudport's billing and see an elevated token consumption in the two-day window and significant p95 spikes that line up with our infra throttling events. I think a two-part offer would be reasonable:

1) Usage forgiveness credit equal to 30% of the measured usage during the incident window (to reflect degraded experience but avoid a full write-down).
2) One complimentary month of dedicated burst capacity (to offset their immediate scaling risk while we roll fixes).

We should present this as an executive-approved goodwill allowance that requires Marissa's sign-off since it exceeds the $50k ad-hoc credit threshold. Details:
- Estimated credit impact: ~$42,000 based on current rates.
- Proposed approval path: Marissa approves; Finance notified; bill adjustment in Feb billing cycle.

I'm attaching a short doc with the numbers. If approved I'll draft a succinct offer email for Samantha that includes terms (no admission of fault; limited to the Jan 12–13 window; one-time offer).

Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- proposed-goodwill-offer.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:40:00 -0800

Thanks for the analysis and the estimate. After reviewing with finance and legal, I can approve the following executive goodwill package:

- A usage allowance equal to 30% of measured consumption during Jan 12–13 (apply as a billing credit on the Feb invoice).
- One complimentary month of Dedicated burst capacity (applied to Cloudport account, valid for 90 days).
- Offer language must include: no admission of liability; limited to the Jan 12–13 incident window; one-time, non-precedent-setting.

Constraints / next steps:
- Finance asks that we cap the write-off at $45,000; if our calculation exceeds that, the residual will be handled as a one-off discount that needs CFO notification.
- Legal wants the customer to sign an acknowledgement email accepting the terms (we don't need a formal amendment).

Karthik, please draft the offer email to Samantha with the numbers and the acknowledgement language. Avery, please confirm the measured usage window and attach the final incident timeline. I'll sign off on the packaged wording once that's in place.

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@cloudport.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 10:50:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed goodwill allowance for Jan 12–13 window — Cloudport

Hi Samantha —

Per our review, here's the executive-approved offer from Redwood:

Offer summary:
- Billing credit: 30% of measured service consumption during Jan 12–13 (applied as a credit on your Feb invoice).
- Complimentary burst month: One month of Dedicated burst capacity added to your account, valid for 90 days from acceptance.
- Cap: Total write-off capped at $45,000; any calculation beyond that will be flagged for CFO review.
- Terms: Limited offer, no admission of liability, one-time, non-precedent. Acceptance requires a short acknowledgement reply from Cloudport confirming acceptance of the terms.

Attached are the numbers that back the 30% estimate. Avery has confirmed the consumption window and incident timeline. Please let us know by close of business Jan 21 if you accept, so we can process the billing credit in time for the Feb cycle.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- proposed-goodwill-offer.docx
- incident-timeline.pdf

Karthik / Marissa / Avery —

We accept the terms as outlined below (billing credit = 30% of measured consumption during Jan 12–13; one complimentary month of Dedicated burst capacity; cap $45,000). We understand the acknowledgement does not constitute admission of fault.

Please proceed with the credit and add the burst month to our account. Once you post the adjustment, please send an updated invoice and a short confirmation note for our finance team.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — we appreciate the partnership.

Samantha Lee
Head of Site Reliability, Cloudport
